name: Saint Rita of Cascia
history: A wife, mother, widow and Augustinian nun of Cascia in Umbria. Tradition says she bore an unhappy marriage with patience, forgave her husband’s murderers and brought peace between feuding families before entering the convent, where she received a wound from a thorn of the crown of Christ. She is the patron of impossible causes and difficult marriages.
life: Most of what we know of Rita comes from tradition written down after her death, but it has been loved for centuries. She was born at Roccaporena, near Cascia, and married young to Paolo Mancini, a man given to violence. By her patience and prayer, it is said, he was changed. He was murdered in a feud, and Rita forgave his killers, but her two sons vowed revenge; she prayed that they would rather die than commit murder, and both died of illness soon after. She asked to enter the Augustinian convent of Saint Mary Magdalene at Cascia and was refused three times, until she had reconciled the families involved in the feud. In the convent she lived in prayer and obedience, and around 1442 a wound like that of a thorn opened in her forehead and stayed with her for fifteen years. Roses are blessed on her feast.
prayerTo: Saint Rita, you bore suffering in marriage and loss with patience, and chose forgiveness over revenge. Pray for those in hard marriages, for families divided by anger, and for all who face what seems impossible. Help me to forgive, to make peace, and to trust God with what I cannot change. Amen.
penance: Pray today for a marriage or family you know to be in difficulty. Take the first step toward peace in a quarrel of your own.
meditation: She would not enter the convent until she had made peace between the families who had killed her husband. What reconciliation is God waiting for before you go further?
